CausalChain: DNA promoter hypermethylation suppresses CLDN18.2 transcription -> Treatment with hypomethylating agents reverses this silencing -> Increased CLDN18.2 mRNA leads to elevated protein expression and cell-surface localization -> Enhanced epitope availability improves binding of CLDN18.2-specific immunotherapies (eg, monoclonal antibodies, CAR-T cells) -> Strengthened immune-mediated tumor cell lysis leads to improved therapeutic outcomes
Hypothesis: Pharmacological demethylation of the CLDN18.2 promoter can upregulate its expression in tumors with low antigen levels, thereby sensitizing them to CLDN18.2-targeted immunotherapies and improving clinical responses.
Abstract: Emerging data indicate that CLDN18.2, a tight junction protein uniquely expressed in normal and select malignant tissues (notably gastric cancers), is modulated by epigenetic mechanisms such as DNA methylation. This review provides a synthesis of current advances in CLDN18.2‐targeted therapies including monoclonal antibodies, CAR‐T cells, and bispecific constructs, while highlighting that differential expression patterns driven by alterations in epigenetic regulation may affect therapeutic efficacy. Here, we propose a novel strategy in which pharmacological demethylation upregulates CLDN18.2 expression in tumors with suboptimal antigen levels, thereby enhancing the binding and cytotoxic potential of CLDN18.2‐targeted immune interventions. The proposed approach may open new avenues to extend the clinical utility of CLDN18.2‐targeted therapies to tumor subsets with low basal expression.
